claims.text: Maintaining a single-phase solid solution constitutes both chemical and structural stability.
HEA nanoparticle stability is governed by the balance among configurational entropy, pairwise mixing enthalpies, and kinetic diffusion barriers.
High configurational entropy favors a disordered, single-phase state.
Strong attractive or repulsive pairwise interactions drive atomic ordering, clustering, or segregation.
Kinetic diffusion barriers delay or suppress ordering, clustering, and segregation.
Microstructural transitions occur when the enthalpic driving force exceeds entropic stabilization and atomic rearrangement is kinetically accessible.
Local ordering, clustering, or surface segregation compromises the stability of the initially homogeneous solid solution.
Changing Al content can alter lattice ordering and produce transitions among single-phase FCC, mixed FCC+BCC, and single-phase BCC configurations.
Adjusting or increasing Al content introduces significant pairwise mixing-enthalpy differences.
Nanoparticles whose constituent pairs have near-zero or modest mixing enthalpies will remain disordered and single-phase throughout 473–1923 K.
The low-mixing-enthalpy nanoparticles will retain their expected catalytic and thermoelectric properties throughout the temperature range.
Nanoparticles with stronger pairwise interactions, such as those produced by increased Al content, will develop local ordering, clustering, or surface segregation at some temperatures.
Ordering, clustering, or segregation will be detectable through diffraction-peak shifts, new diffraction features, TEM, or EDS mapping.
Structural rearrangements caused by stronger interactions will produce changes in catalytic or thermoelectric performance.
The proposed mechanism applies under both reactive catalytic atmospheres and inert or controlled thermoelectric-testing atmospheres.
Very large positive or negative mixing enthalpies can overwhelm entropic stabilization and promote phase separation or ordering.
Reactive environments can drastically enhance diffusion and thereby invalidate the predicted stability behavior.
Surface oxidation and support interactions may influence nanoparticle stability.

contradictions.description: Both sets are called equiatomic, but the modified set is also defined by increasing or adjusting one element; unless compensating changes and a near-equiatomic tolerance are specified, the modified set is not equiatomic.

The mechanism allows even the modified material to remain homogeneous when diffusion is sluggish or the enthalpic driving force is insufficient, yet the falsification rule treats stability of both sets as decisive falsification without establishing that rearrangement was kinetically accessible and the enthalpic threshold was exceeded.
